utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weiner, are you ready for your examination?

utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But before that, we wanted to tender some exhibits, rather than start and tender them while the witness is speaking -- is testifying. We have agreements on two maps and 85 photographs, and we want to tender the photographs in a lump group and the two maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. If there's no disputes concerning of the admission of those documents, I would like to say that these documents are admitted. Are you going to read the number of those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, I will at this time. We'll start off with the two maps. The first one is from the 65 ter. It's numbered 149. It has an ERN number of 0363-9619. That's the large map behind us, the very large one. One moment, Your Honour. It's the very large map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry. So the court deputy will inform us about the court number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, I apologise to you for this very boring practice. Frankly speaking, it is something new to me too. And are you ready to answer any questions put to you by Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Weiner, are you ready for any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed. Examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'd like to show you this sheet of paper and ask you to look at it, please. Sir, on that sheet of paper, it says "Witness A." There's a number "1" there. Is that your name next to number "1"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a number "2" on that sheet of paper. Is that your date of birth next to number "2"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally there is a number "3" on that sheet of paper. Is that your place of birth next to number "3"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that this piece of paper has to be shown to the Defence team. If there's no objections to this sheet of paper, we'll admit it into the evidence

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May that be held under seal and confidential, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It's under seal and confidential.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P87, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session so I can just bring out a few personal details about the witness. And this will probably be the only time we'll need private session for this witness. For a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in the year 1993, were any members of your immediate family serving in the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any members of your immediate family wearing a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of -- any members of your immediate family have a gun or rifle in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No, not that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment. May the witness be shown P86 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognize that photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just wait a moment until the Defence gets the photograph on their screen. It will take a few days, Your Honour, to get used to the new system. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognize that photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you recognize that as?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: This is the village of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that a fair and accurate representation of Grabovica as it appeared in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Well, from this viewpoint, yes. There are a few new buildings built after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in general, is that a fair and accurate representation of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the river that runs through the middle, what's the name of that river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Neretva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we'll move on now, but we'll go back to that picture in a while. In 1993, what was the ethnic make-up of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: It was a Croatian village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the age of the people who lived there, were they mostly families, young people, old people? What was the age of the people that lived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: In general, they were older people with families. There were a few children, including my brother, my sister, and me. But for the most part, they were elderly people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the early part of the year 1993, were there any soldiers guarding that village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The Croatian army did guard it, but they changed shifts from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have many soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were never very many of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the spring of 1993, what happened to the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: One morning, at dawn, shooting began. The shooting woke us up. It went on for quite a long time. When it got light, we came out of the house and we could see the road. Then we saw a self-propelled gun going along the road, and then the turret opened and a green flag with a crescent moon and star could be seen. It then became clear to us that Grabovica had been taken by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of what ethnic group were the soldiers in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to the small number of soldiers that were protecting the village prior to the Bosnian army taking it over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Some were killed and some fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the occupation by the Bosnian army between, let's say, April and September, was anyone in your family, immediate family, harmed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: At the beginning, they took my father away because he was middle-aged. They thought he was a soldier. But a few days later they brought him back. Then they took him away again, telling us that they would never bring him back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he brought back, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: He was brought back six or seven days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he remain on your farm up to September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: He was at home all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other -- were there any other men at your home during that time, between April and September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No, just our family members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just your father and grandfather.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than your father being questioned and then being brought back, was anyone in your family harmed during that period, from the spring to September, to the beginning of September? Was anyone harmed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: In that period, there was looting. When they came to our house, if they liked something, they would take it away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was anyone physically harmed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No. One night they came at night. They wanted something. I don't know what. But you could hear a lot of noise. That's what woke me up. But then it got quiet again very quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to September. What happens in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The soldiers changed. I saw three buses - there may have been more, but maybe not - with a jeep at their head. They were full of soldiers. And when they settled in the village, the atmosphere in the village changed. Very often there was shooting, shouting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that the atmosphere changed when these new soldiers arrived. Could you explain again how it changed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Very often there was shooting. You could hear gunfire. You could hear noise, shouting. In the previous months, it had happened on occasion but not so often. It seemed as if they were celebrating something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what army did these soldiers belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move to September 9th. Could you tell us what happened on or about September 9th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Three soldiers approached our house, entered the courtyard, and asked us whether we had any livestock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe these soldiers, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: One of them was wearing a white T-shirt and military trousers belonging to a uniform. He was rather tall. He had dark hair. Behind him was one wearing a waistcoat and he had a knife in a sheathe in the waistcoat pocket. And I don't remember what the third one looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of what army did these three soldiers belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when they came to your house, who was home? Who was there at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I was there, my brother, my sister, my father, mother, grandmother, and grandfather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when they asked if you had any livestock, did someone answer them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They asked my father to go with them and to show them where the livestock was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your father go with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: He was afraid, so he refused to go with them alone. My grandfather and grandmother and mother went with him, and they were holding hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did they go to? Where were the livestock located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They took the path towards the stable, which is 20 or 30 metres from the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: My mother then went halfway there, and then she returned to the house. Then you could hear a loud burst of fire. I then asked her whether she wanted us to go and hide somewhere, to go and take shelter somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said you heard a loud burst of fire. From what direction did you hear that burst of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: From the direction where the cowshed was located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who in your family had gone into that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: My grandfather, my grandmother, and my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "the cowshed," are you referring to the stable?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us again, what did you say to your mother at that point, when you heard the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: She returned to prepare lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You heard some shooting, and you said something to your mother about hiding. Could you tell us about that? After you heard the shooting, what did you say to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I asked her whether she would like to take shelter until the shooting ceased, but she said it wasn't necessary to take shelter because soldiers had come and gone before and nothing of any significance had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you and your brother do at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: My brother and I took shelter in the vicinity of the house, above the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do once you got to the shelter? When you say "shelter," were you inside or were you outside? Can you give us an idea?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Outside -- outside and above the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We stayed there for a while. We then descended to the house again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, behind the house, did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: You could still hear shooting for a while. And from the location where I was with my brother, we saw a soldier taking a cow of ours through a meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that after the shooting that you saw a cow taking a soldier through the meadow, one of your cows from the meadow [sic].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do next? You see the soldier with the cow. What do you do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We then returned to the house again, to the yard in front of the house. And as far as I can remember, one of the windows had been shattered. The house was in quite a mess. We called out the names of our family members, not too loudly, but no one responded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any members of your family in that house? Could you repeat the answer, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: At that point in time, no one was in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you enter your grandmother's house, which was next to yours -- or your grandparents' home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there anyone in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about in the yard area? Was there anyone out there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I gave you a sheet of paper, could you draw a diagram of your yard or farm with the houses and the barn that you referred to and the area where you hid? Could you do that for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what those objects are.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: This is my grandparents' house, and this was our house. But they were together. Those were our houses. These two points represent my brother and myself when we took shelter. This is the path we used. You can go up this way. And you arrive at a point above the house. This is the yard. There is a fence here. The path leading to the cowshed. These are the two cowsheds

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you put the number "1" next to your house, please, with a pencil or a pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the number "2" next to your grandparents' house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put the number "3" next to the stable or the cowshed, however you want to describe it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the number "4" next to the second cowshed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the area to the right of number 3, the cowshed, is that a yard? Is that the yard in front of the stable or ... That area to the right, yes. What is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: This is the path that leads to the cowshed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put a "5" next to the path that leads to the cowshed, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there a yard in front of that cowshed or -- or a stable, however you want to refer to it? Is there a yard in front of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Inaudible response].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's answer wasn't audible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The interpreter couldn't hear your answer. Was there a path -- I'm sorry, was there a yard or dirt area in front of the cowshed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No. There is a yard in front of the house. That's the only place where there's a yard. There's a room which can be used as an axis route, but it's not a yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, to the right of your home, there is a criss-cross picture. Is that a gate, or what is that? To the right, to the right of number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. That's a gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you put a number "6" by the gate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, could you put a number "7" in that area where you were hiding, you and your brother hid.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get back to that in a while. Thank you. Actually, you can sit down, Madam. You can sit down. Now, sir, let's go back for a few minutes. You told us that the soldiers first arrived. Can you show us -- why don't you show us while it's there where the soldiers were when they first arrived. If you could show us on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They were here, in this yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point -- could you use the pointer to point it out, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that the witness is pointing to an area between the two homes, 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you show us the path that your father, grandfather, grandmother, and mother and sister took towards that -- towards that stable.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: This is the path they took.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the record reflect that they went from the houses down and then took a path right along number 5, the pathway to the barn, a right angle basically that they took.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you were there with your brother. Where were you with your brother when the others left? To go to the barn.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I was in front of the house with my brother. Then my mother returned to prepare lunch. I then asked her whether she wanted to hide when we heard the burst of fire. She said it wasn't necessary. She said that quite a lot of them had already been there and nothing of any significance had ever happened. And then my brother and I took this path and went above the house, and we stayed there for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that he and his brother were in the area between the two homes, between 1 and 2 on that diagram. They spoke with their mother there. And they then went through -- went up behind the house through gate number 6 and to area number 7 along the path. I'd like to offer that diagram at this time, Your Honour. Could you sign that and date that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, please do not sign on that video projector. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that this document is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P88, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There's no need to place that under seal. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because there's a signature of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like you to look at two photographs -- thank you. I'd like you to look at two photographs which are now exhibits, Prosecution Exhibits 22 and 84. Could you look at 22 first, P22.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's P22 and then look at P84.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognize that first photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while they're getting the second one, what was it? Do you recognize the second photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are those photographs of, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Those are photographs of our houses. In a fairly damaged state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But was that the position of the houses back in 1993, right next to each other, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that taken from the front or from the rear or the side? What angle is that taken from? We're looking at P84.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: From the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you indicated before you were looking at the pictures and drew the diagram, you said that you went to the house, you went to both houses, and you couldn't find anyone from your family. What did you and your brother do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We then took the same path. We went above the house, right above. Then we were spotted by a soldier. As far as I can remember, he had some sort of a scarf on his head. When we saw him, we started running. There was shooting from that direction. I don't know whether he was firing in our direction or not. I wouldn't know. But we ran off in the direction of the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you remain in the woods for a while after you ran off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you hear anything while you were in the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: There was a lot of shooting in the village that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We descended to the house, about 50 or 60 metres from the house, and from that position you could see the front part of the cowshed and of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see anything from where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: From that position, we saw that there was a sort of pink cover that we had in the house in front of the cowshed and something had been covered with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "pink cover," are you referring to some sort of bedlinen or a table cloth or curtains or ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Well, it was like a sheet that is used as bedding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said it was in front of the cowshed or the stable, or what I refer to as a stable. Which cowshed? The first one or the second one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: In the first one. The first one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and your brother ever learn what was under that table cloth -- or, I'm sorry, what was under that pinkish sheet?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. There's an objection here. The topic may be a legitimate one to cover in questions, but it better be made clear whether he learned it via his own knowledge or via words, before the question is asked in that general -- in that general way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we might come to that point, and I believe Mr. Weiner will lead us to that point. We'll allow this question to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Right now we're asking -- it's a general question. We'll be in far more specifics later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and your brother ever learn what was below that pink sheet that was in front of the cowshed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was below the pink sheet, sir? Please tell the Judges. What was it covering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: My mother and my sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you stood 50 metres in front of the barn, were you able to see the area in front of your house, in the yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any members of your family in the area of the barn, the house, or the yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the voices of any members of your family in the areas of the house, yard, or barn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown that diagram again, number 88, please, Prosecution's Exhibit P88. [Microphone not activated] ... could you place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please show the Court first where you saw the bodies of your mother and sister lying under that pink sheet.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you put an "8" next to that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Nothing further on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, what did you do next? Tell the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We then returned to the woods because that's where we felt safest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hear anything at the time, while you were in the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: All one could hear was shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We wandered around aimlessly. Occasionally we would sit down. We didn't know where to go or what to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you decide to go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: After a certain period of time, we decided to go to the house of our first neighbour in the village, whose name was (redacted). When we arrived at a point above the house, I saw something like a blue rag, as they say. I saw this from a distance. And I told my brother to wait for me and descended to see what it was. When I had approached the fence, the fence that was behind the house and where you would enter the yard in which our neighbour, (redacted) had chickens, I saw him prostrated on the ground and there was a huge hole in his head. When I saw this, I turned around and ran back to my brother. I told him what I had seen, and we then ran back to the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he bleeding when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: His head was all bloody with a big hole in this part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: In civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wearing a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No. No, none of the Croats in ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said none of the Croats. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: None of the Croats at that time in the village would wear a uniform. They would have been killed immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us his approximate age.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, he was about 55, between 55 and 60 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what ethnic group he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: He was an ethnic Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of what religion was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Roman Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Since this is the first session, I was just wondering when the break period or when would you prefer the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let's come to 4.00. Then we'll make a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that we have to go to the private session for this purpose. Let's go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weiner, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Registrar, could you please show the witness quickly photographs P26 and 27, five seconds of each. Could you look at them, please. And now 27, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recognize -- just first tell me yes or no -- do you recognize those two photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are those photographs of the home of the neighbour - without saying the neighbour's name - who you saw lying on the ground with a hole in his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you ran off to your -- you ran off to your brother after that, you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you tell him what you had seen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just tell us what happened next. What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: After that, we ran to the woods, and we were crossing part of the hill, and there two soldiers spotted us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. They yelled for us to come down. They told us to come down from the hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you meet them somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: First we refused to come down. Then one of the soldiers shouted to us, "Come down or we'll shoot." Then we went down and we met them on a meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were these -- from what army were these soldiers from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness see Exhibit P25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the area where you met the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you make any requests of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: First we told them what had happened during the day. We told them who we were. Then we asked them to take us to our house so that they could see for themselves what had happened and so that we could take some things from our house which we needed, clothes and such like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did they agree to take you to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did something happen when you got close to the barn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: When we approached the barn, from where I was standing you could see part of that pink sheet. And then the soldier whom they called Rambo went up there, and he said, "Don't go near there. There are corpses there." Then he entered the cowshed. He came out quickly, and he said, "Don't go in here either. There are corpses in here too."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did they bring you to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Then they took us to the house by the lower path, below the house, leading up to the gate behind the house. And from there you can enter the house. That's the route we took. We took the things we needed, and then we returned by the same route.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you and your brother walk the same route as you left the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: When we were leaving the house, he went through the courtyard and I went below the house with the two soldiers. He ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet your brother moments later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: When we met a few moments later, he approached me and told me that underneath the sheets were my mother and my sister and that they were covered up to about here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First let's take a step back. Under what sheet? Are you referring to the pink sheet, the pinkish-colour sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And first did he say how he knew it was your mother and your little sister under that pink sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: You could see the upper part of their -- of their faces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he show you what part of the faces that he could see? You said he -- they were covered up to here, you said. Did he show you with his hand a portion of the face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The upper part of the faces could be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, where did you go next, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The soldiers then took us to Pero Lagar's [phoen] house. That's what they called him. You can show me the photograph, and then I'll explain this to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll show you the photograph in a short while, but -- they took you there, and what happened while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: When we arrived there, the soldiers were somewhat surprised. They asked us who we were, how it is that we were there. We then told them what had happened during the day, and they then said that this is something that the Ustasha had done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Our cow was tied up there in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's just step back one second. The soldiers, the soldiers of what army, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they said that the Ustashas had done this. What were they referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They were referring to the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does "Ustasha" mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Well, it's a sort of derogatory term for the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they say that the Ustashas had done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They said that the Ustasha had come and they had killed people in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what people were they referring to? What people were you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They were referring to a people in the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, when you -- they said the -- excuse me. They said the Ustashas had done this. What were you talking about? What did you tell them that they blamed the -- the Croatians for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: When I told them that they had killed everyone in our house, that they had killed my family, they said that they hadn't done that; they said that the Ustasha had arrived, that the Ustasha had killed my family, and they had then left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned a cow. You also asked them about a cow. Can you just briefly tell us what that was about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Our cow was tied up in front of that house. It was in the meadow. That's the same cow that I saw a soldier taking away. And I asked them what the cow was doing there, how come the cow was there. And they said that the cow had just turned up on its own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, were you fed while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. We asked them for food, since we were pretty hungry. We hadn't had anything to eat that day, and night was gradually falling. They then took us into the house, and they gave us something to eat there. There were quite a few soldiers in the room. They were sitting around us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did they put you to bed after you ate, sir, you and your brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They then took us to a room in which we could sleep, and about 15 or 20 minutes later two soldiers came in. One was in civilian clothes, and the other was in uniform. They called him by the nickname Celo, and he asked us who we were, what had happened to us, and where we were from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We then answered the questions he had put to us, and he then left the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this house that you referred to, where you spent the night, was that in the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could photograph 2353 be placed on the screen. Sorry, that would be Exhibit 86, P86.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that house where you spent the night and where you met this person named Celo depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please circle that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to offer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I guess there's no objections, so it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be In-Court Exhibit IC003.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you met Celo, did you tell him what had occurred that day to your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you speak with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, not for very long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you tell him that your family had been killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next morning, did something happen early in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Early in the morning, a soldier entered the room and he told us to get dressed because Celo wanted to see us. After we had got dressed, we went to where he was waiting for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what village was he waiting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: In the village of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: He then asked us whether we could recognise any of the soldiers who had done what they had done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "done what they had done," what did he say? What was he referring to? Or what were the exact words he used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: He was referring to the soldiers who had committed the crime. He asked me whether I recognised any of those who were present in our house that morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "crime," killed your family? Is that the crime you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- were there soldiers at that location, other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: There were quite a few soldiers there. Some were sitting at a table in front of the house. They were drinking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these were soldiers from what army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do? Did you identify anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a reason that you didn't identify anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I didn't want to look at anyone very carefully because even if I had recognised someone, I think I would have been killed on the spot, because if they were able to kill my four-year-old sister, why would they not want to kill me? So I said that I could not see anyone there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did Celo have any conversation with you and your brother after -- after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: He then asked us where we had other family members, in which places. He asked us who we had. We said we had an uncle in Jablanica and an aunt in Mostar. He asked us who we wanted to go to stay with. We said we would like to go to my uncle's in Jablanica. He then put us in a car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they bring you somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They drove us to Donja Jablanica, to Rogica's [phoen] house. Someone they would call Alispago was in the passenger seat. He seemed to be some kind of a bodyguard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how long did you stay at that house? How many days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: 12 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they didn't bring you directly to your uncle's on that first date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could the witness please be shown Exhibit P76.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognize what's depicted in that photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The house in the middle is the house in which I spent 12 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the fifth or sixth day of that stay, did something happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. Zulfikar Alispago, Zuka, who was a commander at the time, he took us to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he take you in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: He took us to our house in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did he take you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I think he wanted to show us where the bodies had been, probably in order to confuse us, because by that day all the evidence had been concealed. I visited the places where they had been, and it wasn't possible to see any traces there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you enter the barn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any corpses in the barn? Any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That area in front of the barn where your mother and little sister laid covered partially by a pink sheet, were either they or the pink sheet still present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No. The bodies weren't there and nor was the pink sheet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any members of your family there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after 12 days, did they take you somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: After 12 days, they asked me whether I wanted to see my uncle, and I said that I did. They then took us to my uncle's, and we did not return to Donja Jablanica from there. We stayed there until the 1st of March, 2004. And then we went to Mostar, with a prisoner exchange. We spent one night in the museum where the ABiH was keeping Croatian civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. You said you were exchanged on the 1st of March, 2004. Is that the proper date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I think so. I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in the year 2004 or was it earlier than that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: 1993. I apologise if I made a slip. The 1st of March, 1993 -- 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were sent to Mostar as part of an exchange programme in 1994. Now, sir, later that year did you have the occasion to visit the hospital in Split?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. I went to the hospital in Split to identify corpses there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go with someone? Did you go with your uncle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you speak with a doctor in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. The doctor asked me what sort of trousers my father was wearing on the day that he was killed. I then told him that he was wearing chequered trousers. He then brought me a sample and asked me whether this fitted the description, and I said that it did. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also on that date, did your uncle view and identify bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that be expunged from the record that goes to the public. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He recognised -- you said his father. Did he recognise your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I identified my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your uncle also make that identification or confirm that identification of your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a funeral held for your father and grandfather after their bodies were identified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, were the bodies of your mother, grandmother, and four-year-old sister ever recovered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Those bodies were never found. They haven't been found to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, would the witness just excuse me and the Court excuse me while I lift the podium up and arrange and prepare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. You are not going to conduct a long cross-examination, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I indicate it will be both as long as necessary and relatively short at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at the time when the village was -- was reoccupied by the Army of Bosnia on the 5th -- on the 9th of May of 1993, did you notice an individual called Nihad fighting for that army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the initial fright of that occupation, did you and your family both become accustomed to seeing soldiers in the village of Grabovica from time to time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Given the circumstances, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whether any of those soldiers belonged to a unit called Celo's Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I only heard that name later. How could a 10-year-old know anything about that at the time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the fact that you simply cannot recall any of the names of the different units at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I didn't know the units at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Were soldiers living nearby to Grabovica in the hydroelectric plant at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We never strayed very far from the house. Our parents wouldn't allow us to do so. The hydroelectric plant is some distance away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. As to the soldiers that you saw in the village from time to time, are you unable to say where it was they resided?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I think that they had found accommodation in houses or in -- in the hut on the left bank, which I could show you on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we go to the photograph, are you referring to the barracks-like structure that was on the left bank of the village opposite the houses on your side of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P3, which is this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the foreground of that photograph, can you see the -- the hut to which you're referring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If that exhibit can be removed again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Was there a -- an area up the mountain from your dwelling place known as Diva Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take to walk from Grabovica to Diva Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I never went there on foot, but I think that it would take about an hour or an hour and a half to get there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between May and September of 1993, was Diva Grabovica located close to the front line of the fighting parties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go there in that period yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period between May and September 1993, did you see Marinko Dreznjak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No. As I have said, I never went very far from the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall him visiting you at the house in that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I don't recall him visiting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When the troops from Sarajevo arrived, did you hear a great deal of shooting, shouting, and general noise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the past, had the soldiers from the Bosnian army sometimes fired off guns for no apparent reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the troops from Sarajevo arrived, you indicated in evidence earlier that it sounded as if they were celebrating. Did it sound to you as if -- I withdraw that question. Did you draw that conclusion about celebration partly from the fact of hearing the gunfire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Because of the atmosphere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But the gunfire was a part of that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Well, there was a war on. Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And in short, merely because you heard gunfire, you didn't draw a conclusion that anyone was being killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: At what stage? At what stage? I'd object. Upon arrival?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the -- the situation is very clear here, you know. We know -- we know when the celebration is. Let us see whether the witness could answer this question or not. If not, maybe Mr. Morrissey could ask a more specific question in that direction. But at least I understand the question and the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, in any event, I will clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yeah, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pardon me, Witness. I'll ask the question again in a different way. At the time when you heard the gunfire that you connected with celebrating, you did not think anyone was being shot and killed at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I can't answer this very precisely. I can't recall my thought processes at the time, but that was the impression I had, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And -- very well. Now, on the morning of the 9th of September, you noticed three soldiers at your property. And what I want to ask you is: Did you see them approach along a path, or did you just notice them after they arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We saw them as they were going from the gate to the courtyard, as the gate is not very far from the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And when they approached you, they did not initially appear to be unfriendly or aggressive; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it the case that your mother appeared to you to treat this visit as just another visit by just another group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: We met them in the same way as the previous groups, because we could not imagine what was about to happen. They arrived with the simple question, "Do you have any livestock?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nothing had happened the night before which caused you to have any special caution or fear of these men; is that correct? To your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Nothing happened that would indicate something like this could happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All you had heard in the previous day was shouting, shooting, and what you've described as celebration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I have very few questions for you about the shootings that you've already described, but I have questions about the men who arrived, and those are the questions I'm going to ask you. Firstly, have you ever been shown photographs of individual people with a view to having you identify the men who came to your farm that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not by the Croatian authorities and not by the Office of the Prosecutor here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been asked whether you knew a man called Haris Rajkic, R-a-j-k-i-c?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Enes Sakrak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I've heard that name. I think I heard that name somewhere or read it in a newspaper. It somehow seems familiar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Prosecutor or any other person identify to you that a man has confessed to shooting your mother and your baby sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I heard that at the court in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been asked about a man called Sead, S-e-a-d - I apologise for the pronunciation - Karagic, K-a-r-a-g-i-c [Realtime transcript read in error "Karadzic"]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No, I've never heard that name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to provide further descriptions of the man who had a headband or a scarf on his head that you saw who might have fired at you after the incidents at your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I don't recall anyone asking me that; although, in the statements, we mentioned him but we only saw him very briefly. It was just a brief glimpse of him before we turned and fled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you -- I'm jumping forward briefly to the following day, when the man named Celo lined up the soldiers. When you looked at those men that were lined up, did you in fact recognise any person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No. But I didn't really want to look at them very carefully. I didn't want to look at them properly, because I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just need -- I need some clarity on this topic. Is your -- do you say that the killers might have been in that line but you didn't look closely, or that the killers definitely were not in that line?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. I'd object to the first half of it, when he asks, "Are you saying -- could the killers might have been in that line," you're asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. You may rephrase your question, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you rule out the possibility that one or more of the killers was in that line or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's just as bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I justify the question if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The witness might be in two states, it seems to me. He might say he look at the men briefly and can say for sure that the killers were not in that line, or he might say he was not looking properly because he didn't want to be seen to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They might have been or they might not have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, I believe that this Bench will evaluate this piece of the evidence, taking into the consideration of the special circumstances at that time as well as the age of this witness at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, returning back to the events on -- at the farmhouse. You then -- having hidden from the three men who were involved in the killings, did you see a fourth man, that being the man with the scarf around his head, or was he one of the three?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The three who came to the house, none of them had a scarf on their head. This one did, so he was a fourth man. Unless of course he put the scarf on in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was obvious to you that this fourth man saw you and noticed you; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, I think our eyes met at one point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you attended at the neighbour's house. Your account is that you -- pardon me. Your account is that you saw one person deceased at that premises; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that's the account that you gave to the investigators from this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the past, have you given an account of seeing more than that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that because of anger or for some other reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Today in the courtroom I said everything I can recollect at this point. It's possible I may have mentioned this, or maybe not, but now I can recall everything that I said today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know a man called Pero and -- and his partner Matija Culjak? Culjak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had not -- where did they live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [In English] Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the path to your house go past the neighbour's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the main path to your house, or are there a number of paths to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: It's the main path.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the path along which the soldiers appeared to come and appeared to go on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: What soldiers do you mean now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The three soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I think they arrived by that path. That's the only way they could have reached the main gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when leaving with the animals, is that the way they appeared to be taking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later you were detected by soldiers and effectively arrested by them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the soldier -- the soldier Rambo permitted you to go back to your premises; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by the time -- soon after that he took you to Pero Maric's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Pero Maric's house appeared by this time to have been constructed --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Pero Lagar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Now, is the name Lagar a family name or is it a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: It's a nickname. His last name is Maric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is. I understand. Very well. Well, were you taken to his home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this house being used as a base by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: In view of the number of soldiers in that house, one might say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the cow that had been taken from your house tied up nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the soldiers talk about it as a base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I can't recall that. But my first impression, when I saw the number of soldiers there, that's what I thought.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near to that house, was there a partially constructed -- perhaps I'll withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P38.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to see a partially constructed white house in that picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that particular house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I think this house was in front of Pero Maric's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Orienting yourself in relation to that photograph, can you point with a pointer the direction of Pero Maric's house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: It was in this direction, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to see -- do you see a white structure hidden in the bushes at the end of -- in the distance of Exhibit P38 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: It's possible that that is the house; although, it doesn't look like a house now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown photograph -- Exhibit P3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have in front of you there a photograph that's --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On the extreme left of that photograph in about the middle, do you see a part of a -- well, perhaps I should ask you the question directly: Is Pero Maric's house to be seen in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes, a bit of it, I think. I think this is the house. And that this is the house on the photograph we just saw. And if you look in this direction, then it's logical that it should be here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In conclusion, therefore, is it safe to say that the -- the wrecked house appears to be within 50 metres of Pero Maric's house at the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I never measured it, but it's possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. All right. Now, in your journey from your home down to that base, you were in the company of Rambo for most or all of that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see the bodies of any other persons in that journey; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst at Mr. Pero Maric's house, you did not see any other bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was obvious to you at all times that the soldiers at Pero Maric's base were trying to put a false appearance on the situation in the village by claiming the killings had been done by other people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes. Because of our age, I think they tried to confuse us or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they fed you food and talked to you nicely; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: They gave us food, but as to the way they addressed us, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's okay. Now, you were approached by a man in civilian clothes and a man in -- a man dressed as a soldier, as you recall. I want to ask you some questions about that. Firstly, did one of those men appear to be the leader of that group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all the others seem to obey?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think the transcript system is down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We're not receiving -- sorry for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have two monitors in front of us, and I believe that I relied on that small screen for the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is counsel's working?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, ours is working. Your Honour, I apologise to the witness and to the Court. Mine appears to be working. Another one we have appears not to be working.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We have one that works. We'll try and work off this. Sorry for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And could I ask at this moment how long your cross-examination will last.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think it's likely to be going not more than another half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe the best way for us is to have our break so that the technicians could have the computer fixed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, is the plan to start the other witness today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll try that, but it seems to me that it's impossible to do that. Because after the break it's almost 6.00. Then Mr. Morrissey will take another 30 minutes. Then we'll have the Judges to ask some questions. So probably we'll not call the next witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May I release the witness, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we'll resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I just correct the transcript -- a matter at transcript T53. I spelled -- the name is K-a-r-a-g-i-c. It's been realised as -- as another individual known to these courts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And I apologise for that delay. Now, I was asking you before the break about the procedure at the Maric house and your encounter with the leader of this group. And what I wanted to ask you is this: You met with three killers relatively early in the morning at your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you wandered -- can I -- may I ask you this: I take it you weren't keeping time with a wristwatch or any other clock device?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw the -- the leader of these soldiers down at Pero Maric's house, was it still light?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: The first time I saw him was when he entered the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A
utterances.text: It was already beginning to get quite dark at that time. In September, well, then you can calculate for yourself what time it might have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
